brief: JPM's October 14 morning briefing strings together several threads. Equity broadening faded into tech weakness, with ASML's light Q3 print seen disappointing on 2027 guidance and 2028 capacity detail; dovish Fed commentary eased global rates even as oil rose on Middle East and Russia/Ukraine escalation. China's September PPI rose 1.1% m/m sa, outpacing consumer prices and squeezing margins amid weak end-demand, while its trade surplus nears $1tn (a record $35bn with the EU); last week's EU/China talks lowered near-term disruption risk and structured dispute handling but left the imbalance itself unresolved beyond EVs, with JPM Econ's base case managed de-escalation over 3-6 months. EU/US banks de-rated through September on valuation rather than earnings concerns even as hedge funds bought US and EU banks into a potential Q4 rebound, and Kian keeps EU banks OW. US CPI is forecast at 0.55% m/m headline (3.6% oya) and 0.18% m/m core (2.4% oya), with global inflation momentum turning higher on goods prices. JPM stays tactically bullish on global equities (long US/Asia vs EU, China A-shares barbell, EM country trades), while its own Positioning Intelligence desk flags HFs buying banks, selling semis, and EU positioning sliding toward the 13th percentile against the US's 46th.
